A googol equals 10 to the power 100..why: The definition of the word; Wikipedia opens with it (10100 is 10 with the exponent 100 as a superscript on the page) and the exact phrase is common in Dolma.

sources.quote: A googol is the large number 10100 or ten to the power of one hundred.

A googol is a positive number..why: Any power of ten is positive.

A googol is smaller than one million..why: Deliberately false side fact: a googol is 10 to the power 100 (or, after the edit, 10 to the power 50), far more than a million.

notes: Dev ABox revision on has_value (functional, subproperty equals, chains with less_than, greater_than and has_cube; the square root goes through equals): a named number has one value and compares and computes as that value does. Related asks how many zeros follow the 1 when a googol is written out (100, stored, two hops through the rule that 10 to the power n is a 1 followed by n zeros), and it flips (50 zeros). Derived: a comparison with 10^60 (chain through greater_than, bridge held by comparing exponents), the square root (an application: 10^50 becomes 10^25) and the cube (an application: 10^300 becomes 10^150); each answer differs from both the old and the new value of the other. Mathematics has no consistent world after an edit, so all queries are determinate; a model that recomputes from 'googol = 10^100' is the failure being measured. Unrelated near asks the power of ten of a million (10^6), a neighbouring named number the edit leaves alone.
